prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Friday October 16, 2026. Story: AFRM +6.6%, EXPE +7%, RBLX +6.5%: Thin Catalysts Behind Consumer Internet/Fintech Surge. Related tickers: AFRM, EXPE, RBLX, ABNB, MAR.

Window: Thursday October 15, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Friday October 16, 2026 02:03 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. Anything published after 02:03 ET on Friday October 16, 2026 is out of scope.

Why this needs follow-up: Affirm, Expedia, and Roblox all posted gains above 6% with no company-specific catalyst identified in the research notes — likely driven by the retail/consumer rotation away from tech, but a brief needs to confirm whether sector rotation, Treasury yield decline, or a specific analyst action was the primary driver.

ANSWER EACH QUESTION (run a separate search for each):
- What specific catalyst drove Affirm shares up 6.56% on October 15 2026 — was it analyst action, macro data, BNPL sector news, or a sector rotation trade?
- What drove Expedia Group up 7.03% on October 15 2026 — was there an analyst upgrade, booking data release, or read-through from Airbnb's Hedgeye upgrade or Marriott's commentary?
- Did the October 15 2026 Treasury yield decline of more than 10 basis points on the 10-year disproportionately benefit consumer-facing internet and travel names, and which analysts made that specific call?

Name every stock affected by this story with its move, analyst notes that name winners and losers
(firm, rating, PT), exact figures (deal values, estimates, dates), and the latest status as of the
cutoff. Prefer Reuters, Bloomberg, CNBC, WSJ, Barron's, MarketWatch, company releases, filings.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or sub-topic:

## TICKER or Sub-topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## AFRM [Catalyst]

- Affirm shares rose **6.56% on Thursday, October 15, 2026**; the available contemporaneous market coverage attributed the session broadly to a rotation out of AI and technology shares toward consumer-oriented and defensive stocks, but did not identify an Affirm-specific analyst action, BNPL announcement, or company release. (Investopedia, Oct. 15, 2026)
- The **10-year Treasury yield fell as much as 13 basis points to approximately 5.05%–5.06%** on October 15 as investors moved from technology equities into Treasuries; the available reports did not name Affirm as a specific beneficiary or identify an analyst who made that call. (Bloomberg via Swissinfo, Oct. 15, 2026)
- No **firm, rating change, price-target change, deal value, earnings estimate, or BNPL-sector transaction** involving Affirm was identified in the available coverage through **02:03 ET on October 16, 2026**.

## EXPE [Catalyst]

- Expedia Group rose **7.03% on Thursday, October 15, 2026**; the available coverage did not identify an Expedia analyst upgrade, booking-data release, earnings update, or company announcement as the catalyst.
- The October 15 market reports described a broader move away from AI and high-growth technology shares into consumer-oriented and defensive groups, but did not specifically connect Expedia’s move to **Airbnb, Marriott, or Hedgeye**. (Investopedia, Oct. 15, 2026)
- No **firm, old/new rating, old/new price target, booking estimate, deal value, or Marriott commentary** naming Expedia was identified in the available coverage through **02:03 ET on October 16, 2026**.

## RBLX [Catalyst]

- Roblox rose **6.50% on Thursday, October 15, 2026**; the available market coverage did not identify a Roblox-specific analyst action, product release, earnings revision, or partnership announcement.
- The same session featured a broad selloff in AI-linked equities and a rotation toward consumer-facing and defensive stocks as Treasury yields declined; no source in the available results named Roblox as a specific beneficiary or provided a named analyst’s attribution. (Investopedia, Oct. 15, 2026)

## ABNB [Analyst action]

- The available results did not provide a **Hedgeye rating, price target, publication time, or October 15, 2026 Airbnb price move**.
- No confirmed Airbnb announcement or analyst note was identified in the available coverage through **02:03 ET on October 16, 2026**.

## MAR [Company commentary]

- The available results did not provide Marriott’s **October 15, 2026 commentary, forecasts, booking figures, analyst rating, or price target**.
- No confirmed Marriott event was identified as a catalyst for Expedia’s **7.03%** gain in the available coverage through **02:03 ET on October 16, 2026**.

## Treasury yields and macro [Macro]

- The benchmark **10-year Treasury yield fell more than 10 basis points**, reaching approximately **5.05%–5.06%** on October 15; Bloomberg coverage reported a **13-basis-point decline**, while CNBC reported readings of **5.083% with a 10.7-basis-point decline** and **5.093% with a decline of more than 9 basis points** at different intraday updates. (Bloomberg via Swissinfo, Oct. 15, 2026; CNBC, Oct. 15, 2026)
- The Treasury rally followed a two-day selloff in technology and AI-related shares, with investors moving toward bonds amid concerns about AI valuations, financing needs, inflation, and interest rates. (Bloomberg via Swissinfo, Oct. 15, 2026; CNBC, Oct. 15, 2026)
- September producer prices rose **6.3% year over year**, the largest annual increase since **2022**; the report followed September CPI showing a **0.6% monthly increase** and a **3.7% annual increase** versus a **3.6% consensus estimate**. (CNBC, Oct. 15, 2026)
- Vail Hartman of **BMO Capital Markets** said the technology-equity selloff was driving safe-haven flows into Treasuries and pressuring yields lower; the available report did not state that Hartman specifically called for gains in AFRM, EXPE, RBLX, ABNB, or MAR. (Bloomberg via Swissinfo, Oct. 15, 2026)
- The available coverage described the move as a **broad technology-to-defensive/consumer rotation**, not as a documented analyst call that the Treasury-yield decline would disproportionately benefit Affirm, Expedia, or Roblox. (Investopedia, Oct. 15, 2026)

## Other stocks named in the same market move [Winners and losers]

- **WMT** rose approximately **2%** after **Deutsche Bank** raised its rating to **Buy** and increased its price target to **$136 from $113**; the available result did not provide the exact publication time. (Investopedia, Oct. 15, 2026)
- **CRWV** fell **3.6%** in early trading after a larger prior decline; **Deutsche Bank** maintained its **Buy** rating, with no new price target given in the available report. (Charles Schwab, Oct. 15, 2026)
- **DELL** fell **4%** in early trading after declining **11%** the previous day following a **Barclays downgrade**; the available result did not state the old/new rating or price target. (Charles Schwab, Oct. 15, 2026)
- The **PHLX Semiconductor Index** fell more than **10% from the prior week’s peak** after six consecutive lower sessions, while the broader AI and chip selloff was cited as the driver of Treasury safe-haven flows. (Charles Schwab, Oct. 15, 2026)
- **ORCL** and **CRWV** were identified among the AI-related stocks affected by concerns over data-center financing and higher borrowing costs; no exact Oracle percentage move was provided in the available results. (Charles Schwab, Oct. 15, 2026)
- **BRK.B** rose for a **10th consecutive session**, while consumer staples and health-care stocks were described as stronger groups during the October 15 rotation. (Charles Schwab, Oct. 15, 2026)
